purpose: Define a conservative, rider-controlled low-speed companion mode for eventual dog-accompanied neighborhood use without using a dog during development qualification.

interpretation: These are initial research limits chosen to be below the existing Learn-mode envelope.
Current slew is only a torque-change proxy; it is not physical jerk authority.
Actual acceleration, jerk, stopping distance, traction, and dog suitability require staged physical qualification.

required_behavior.deadman_or_remote_loss_action: ramp propulsion toward zero with bounded fault-release slew; recommend independent mechanical braking; do not invent automatic traction-power braking authority
required_behavior.overspeed_action: do not increase propulsion; ramp positive drive toward zero with bounded fault-release slew; recommend independent mechanical braking
required_behavior.pack_overvoltage_regen_action: drop regen request immediately to zero and recommend independent mechanical braking

rationale: A lateral leash impulse must not become board steering or a structural load on the vehicle.
Dog-accompanied use adds an unpredictable external moving load and should be introduced only after rider-only low-speed control and stopping are independently qualified.

qualification_ladder.name: host_software
qualification_ladder.exit: host tests cover cap, slew, deadman, overspeed, overvoltage regen removal, and symmetric nominal output

qualification_ladder.name: bench_no_rider
qualification_ladder.exit: future bench setup demonstrates command transitions and fault outputs without road contact

qualification_ladder.name: rider_only_closed_low_speed
qualification_ladder.exit: future closed-course tests establish actual acceleration, jerk, stopping response, remote release behavior, and stability below companion cap

qualification_ladder.name: companion_proximity_no_leash_load
qualification_ladder.exit: future protocol only; not authorized by this specification

non_goals: using software speed limits as a substitute for physical braking
